As the finding of the arbitrator was not questioned by the petitioner with regard to the limitation, the finding had reached finality.

The decision on an issue is said to be final when so far as the court rendering it is concerned, it is unalterable except by resort to such provisions which permit its reversal, modification or amendment.

Similarly final decision would mean a decision which would operate as res judicata between the parties if it is not sought to be modified or reversed by preferring an appeal or a revision or review application as if permitted.
It is not open the petitioner to re-agitate the question of limitation, having failed to question the same under Section 34 when the first arbitral award dated 12.04.2019 was passed.
So, this Court cannot consider whether the respondent No. 1 had approached the respondent No. 2 within time.
